source.title: Parallel Layer Normalization for Universal Approximation
source.authors: Yun-Hao Ni; Yu-He Liu; Wen-Xin Sun; Yi-Tong Tang; Yu-Xin Guo; Pei-Lin Feng; Wen-Jun Wu; Lei Huang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses fixed random labels to compare normalization domains, and reports that fit and clean-label generalization depend on grouping axes and replacement site. Its experiments change the normalization arrangement and do not test the original standard-network settings unchanged.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own fixed-random-label fitting results for CNNs and ViTs. It also reports clean-label accuracy for comparison. The cited Zhang et al. random-label protocol is prior work, not a result row. Results for the broader CNN and ViT grids are shown in figures; only values stated in text or tables are extracted.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures fitting of completely random labels by gradient-trained CNNs and ViTs. Its results bear on V1 and show that complete fitting depends on normalization domain and model setting within the stated training budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the relevant empirical conclusion: normalization domains, grouped axes, replacement sites, and label structure affect fitting and generalization, and greater random-label fitting does not yield comparable clean-label generalization gains. The paper's principal conclusion concerns universal approximation by parallel normalization units.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fixed random labels as in the cited protocol, but varies normalization domains or replacement sites within CNNs and ViTs; it does not reproduce the original unchanged model and training settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Normalization domain and grouped axes; for ViTs, replacement site (all normalization layers versus FFN activations); evaluation task (random-label fitting versus clean-label generalization).

fits_no_version.finding: Improved random-label fitting under grouped replacements yields only small gains, or losses, in clean-label ViT test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization changes that improve memorization capacity need not comparably improve clean-label generalization.

record.problems: CNN Table 2 gives three-seed means without uncertainty values. ViT Table 3 reports the best mean and best single-run values selected independently across configurations, rather than a single matched configuration. The text reports fitting accuracy but not test error on random labels; the broader grids are presented in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No separately attributable numeric rows were extracted from the CNN mixed-axis grid in Figure A1 or the ViT 6,000-example and 20,000-example grids in Figures A4–A5. The text describes these grids but does not give each cell's values in prose; Table 3 provides the stated ViT summary values used above. Clean-label training accuracies from Table 3 are omitted because they do not measure the claim's random-label behavior.

untested.parts: Random-label held-out error at chance; replication of the original architectures and hyperparameters. Architecture choices are varied across comparisons, although each reported configuration is trained directly on random labels.
Relative training time for real versus random labels and convergence slowing across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Intermediate corruption fractions, perfect fitting throughout that sweep, and steadily worsening held-out error.
Controlled effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Incomplete fitting is classified as partial, rather than absent, when accuracy substantially exceeds chance. These finite-budget results do not establish inability to fit with longer training. Figure-grid omissions are already declared in rows_left_out. Missing random-label test error is untested, not itself a scope-limiting result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original cited architectures and training settings unchanged; does not report random-label test error or establish that it is at chance.
Training time and convergence rate as label corruption increases are not reported.
Does not test shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not sweep corruption fractions from none to all or report the proposed smooth relationship between test error and corruption.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Does not report the order in which real-label patterns and noise are learned over training.

relation.reason: The study directly measures training accuracy on completely random labels across controlled CNN and ViT normalization settings.

tranche.reason: Random-label fitting is complete in specified CNN configurations but incomplete in others and in the tested ViT means, showing that V1 needs qualification by normalization setting and training budget.

source_check.notes: CNN outcomes are final accuracies; ViT random-label outcomes use best evaluated accuracies, with configuration maxima for means and single runs selected independently. Chance-level testing after random-label training and V2–V6 are not established by these comparisons.

statements.correction: Table 2: LN fitting accuracy 24.6%; best conventional GN 95.8%; depth-4, width-128 normalization-only CNN; 50,000 fixed random CIFAR-10 labels; three-seed means after 200 SGD epochs. Label for this study: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The challenges label is inappropriate for this study: the LN and GN results show incomplete fitting, rather than an absent or reversed effect.
